title: Classic Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Boil pasta. Fry guanciale. Whisk eggs and cheese. Combine hot pasta with guanciale, remove from heat, quickly stir in egg mixture to create a creamy sauce. Top with black pepper.
tips: Never add cream to authentic carbonara. The creaminess comes from the emulsion of starchy pasta water, melted fat from guanciale, and eggs.

title: Perfect Roasted Chicken
instructions: Dry the chicken thoroughly. Rub with butter, salt, and herbs. Stuff cavity with lemon. Roast at 425°F (220°C) until internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
tips: For extra crispy skin, dry brine the chicken with salt in the fridge uncovered overnight. Let it rest for 15 minutes before carving to keep juices inside.

title: Basic Vinaigrette
instructions: Whisk 1 part vinegar with 3 parts olive oil. Add a teaspoon of Dijon mustard to help emulsify. Season to taste.
tips: If your salad dressing is too sharp, add a pinch of sugar or a dash of honey to balance the acidity.

title: Fluffy Scrambled Eggs
instructions: Whisk eggs well. Melt butter in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Add eggs and stir constantly with a spatula until softly set.
tips: Remove the pan from the heat slightly before the eggs look done; they will continue cooking in the residual heat of the pan.

title: Crispy Roasted Potatoes
instructions: Parboil potatoes in water with salt and a half teaspoon of baking soda. Drain and toss vigorously to rough up edges. Roast at 450°F (230°C) with olive oil until golden and crispy.
tips: The baking soda breaks down the exterior of the potato, creating a starchy slurry that turns incredibly crunchy in the oven.

title: Fixing Salty Food
tips: If a soup or stew is too salty, you can add water, unsalted broth, or a squeeze of lemon juice to balance it. Contrary to popular belief, adding a raw potato does not significantly absorb salt.
